defects.quote: derived facts confirm the transaction sample counts (100) sum to the overall count (100)
defects.why: The input has no derived facts, and matching totals across overall and transaction scopes do not establish a shared sample population.

defects.quote: removing or adding a single errored sample changes the pass/fail outcome
defects.why: Adding an errored sample leaves the rate above 1%, and removing one from both the error count and denominator also leaves it above 1%.

notes: The verdict and investigation steps are useful, but the scope claim and arithmetic could mislead an operator.
It preserves the verdict and key numbers while prioritizing checks that can be verified from source records.

defects.quote: both recorded errors correspond to the checkout transaction
defects.why: Equal aggregate counts across different scopes do not establish that the same samples produced the errors.

defects.quote: All error counts and the policy check are whole-run values
defects.why: The evidence also contains a transaction-scoped checkout error count.

notes: It gives useful source-record checks but asserts unsupported checkout attribution and omits validity and coverage.

defects.quote: remediation is needed on the error source rather than on the run infrastructure
defects.why: VALID run status and COMPLETE coverage do not rule out a load or test infrastructure cause for the errors.

defects.quote: removing the error source is the only path to a PASS on a subsequent run
defects.why: A subsequent run could pass through variation or an intentional policy correction without a proven error source being removed.

notes: The core verdict and sample inspection advice are sound, but its remediation claims are too certain.
It preserves the verdict and scope limits and offers practical checks, though a single rerun provides limited evidence about flakiness.

defects.quote: the two recorded errors are the entire error population in these scopes
defects.why: Matching aggregate counts do not establish that the overall and checkout scopes contain the same two error samples.

notes: Its later caveats recognize the scope ambiguity, but the summary makes an unsupported cross-scope identity claim.
